segments.englishExplanation: The speaker introduces himself and says hello.
The speaker begins addressing the other character with a brief pause.
The speaker states the name of the character he is addressing.

segments.text: You are so much more than just a sheep, aren't you? Oh yeah?
segments.englishExplanation: The speaker suggests that Frank has depth beyond being an ordinary sheep, ending with a question tag and a playful reaction.
segments.turkishExplanation: Sen sadece bir koyundan çok daha fazlasısın, değil mi? Öyle mi?

segments.englishExplanation: A rhetorical or skeptical question asking how the other could possibly know that.

learningPoints.englishExplanation: Used to emphasize that someone or something has far greater value, complexity, or qualities than a basic label suggests.
learningPoints.turkishExplanation: Birinin veya bir şeyin basit bir tanımdan ya da sıradan bir durumdan çok daha fazlası veya değerlisi olduğunu vurgulamak için kullanılır.
learningPoints.exampleEn: This project is so much more than just a hobby.
learningPoints.exampleTr: Bu proje sadece bir hobiden çok daha fazlası.

learningPoints.englishExplanation: A conversational challenge used to express skepticism about how someone could possibly have information or insight about something.
learningPoints.turkishExplanation: Karşıdakinin bir konuda bilgi sahibi olamayacağını ima ederek şüpheyle sorulan 'Sen nereden bileceksin ki?' kalıbı.
learningPoints.exampleEn: You've never been there, so how would you know?
learningPoints.exampleTr: Oraya hiç gitmedin ki, nereden bileceksin?

quiz.question: In segment 4, what does the speaker imply by saying Frank is "so much more than just a sheep"?

options.text: Frank has a unique personality beyond being an ordinary animal.
Frank is physically much larger and heavier than other sheep.
Frank belongs to an extremely rare and valuable sheep breed.
Frank requires much more food and daily care than normal.

issues.message: Learning point ifadesi ("so much more than (just)...") segment 4'in transcript metninde literal olarak bulunamadı — pedagojik notation/çekim farkı olabilir, yanlış pozitif olasılığı var.

segments.text: Look at you, you're an adventurer, Frank.
segments.englishExplanation: Remarking warmly that Frank behaves or looks like a daring explorer.
segments.turkishExplanation: Baksana sana, tam bir maceracısın, Frank.

segments.text: Just like me, you're a lone wolf.
segments.englishExplanation: Saying that Frank, just like the speaker, is an independent and solitary character.
segments.turkishExplanation: Tıpkı benim gibi, sen de yalnız bir kurtsun.

segments.text: Tell me, does one choose to be alone?
segments.englishExplanation: Posing a philosophical question about whether people actively decide to live in solitude.
segments.turkishExplanation: Söyle bana, insan yalnız olmayı kendi mi seçer?

segments.englishExplanation: Asserting that people do not deliberately choose loneliness.

segments.text: One doesn't even choose to be a wolf.
segments.englishExplanation: Continuing the thought by stating that one does not even decide their own fundamental nature.
segments.turkishExplanation: İnsan kurt olmayı bile kendi seçmez.

segments.englishExplanation: Doubtfully reconsidering whether people actually might have a choice after all.

vocabulary.gloss: yalnız kurt, kendi başına buyruk kimse

learningPoints.englishExplanation: An idiom used to describe an independent person who prefers doing things alone rather than being part of a group.
learningPoints.turkishExplanation: Başkalarına bağımlı olmadan tek başına hareket etmeyi ve yaşamayı tercih eden kişileri tanımlayan bir deyim.
learningPoints.exampleEn: He has always been a lone wolf who prefers working without a team.
learningPoints.exampleTr: Her zaman bir ekip olmadan çalışmayı tercih eden yalnız bir kurt olmuştur.

learningPoints.englishExplanation: Using the pronoun 'one' as a formal or philosophical way to refer to any person or people in general.
learningPoints.turkishExplanation: Resmi veya felsefi anlatımlarda genel olarak insanları ('insan', 'kişi') kastetmek için kullanılan üçüncü tekil zamir yapısı.
learningPoints.exampleEn: One must be careful when walking alone at night.
learningPoints.exampleTr: İnsan gece yalnız yürürken dikkatli olmalıdır.

quiz.question: In segment 2, what does the phrase 'lone wolf' mean?

options.text: Someone who is independent and prefers being by themselves
Someone who is aggressive and dangerous toward others
Someone who is actively searching for a group to join
Someone who has lost their way in an unfamiliar environment

issues.message: Learning point ifadesi ("generic pronoun 'one'") segment 3'in transcript metninde literal olarak bulunamadı — pedagojik notation/çekim farkı olabilir, yanlış pozitif olasılığı var.

segments.text: Just give me one minute of your precious time.
segments.englishExplanation: A persuasive request asking the listener to spare just a single moment of their valuable time.
segments.turkishExplanation: Değerli vaktinden bana sadece bir dakikanı ayır.

segments.englishExplanation: Questioning the description of their time as 'precious' with surprise or amusement.

segments.text: Yeah, just give me one minute.
segments.englishExplanation: Reiterating the request to have just one minute to talk.
segments.turkishExplanation: Evet, sadece bir dakikanı ver bana.

segments.text: You would have one more minute, wouldn't you? Okay, half. Half of me.
segments.englishExplanation: Trying to persuade the listener with a tag question before immediately bargaining down to half.
segments.turkishExplanation: Bir dakikan daha olurdu, değil mi? Tamam, yarım olsun.

learningPoints.englishExplanation: A tag question using the modal auxiliary 'would' to seek confirmation, agreement, or playfully persuade someone.
learningPoints.turkishExplanation: Karşıdakinden onay almak veya onu ikna etmek amacıyla kullanılan 'olurdu, değil mi?' kalıbındaki soru takısı (tag question).
learningPoints.exampleEn: You would help me if I asked, wouldn't you?
learningPoints.exampleTr: Sorsaydım bana yardım ederdin, değil mi?

quiz.question: In segment 1, what does the speaker mean by the phrase 'precious time'?

options.text: Time that is treated as highly valuable and limited
A scheduled meeting that cannot be cancelled
Free time spent exclusively on relaxation
Extra minutes accumulated after working late

issues.message: Learning point ifadesi ("would ..., wouldn't you?") segment 4'in transcript metninde literal olarak bulunamadı — pedagojik notation/çekim farkı olabilir, yanlış pozitif olasılığı var.
